session: session 7 / H58 (2026-10-10): H58 hypotheses executed and closed; H59-A..E pre-registered
novelty_scope: Compared with the inspected implementations in this repository. No claim of global scientific novelty or exhaustive novelty across every sibling method.

candidates.hypothesis: Multi-scale host-bend damage asymmetry & detrended-elevation scarp relative strike
layers: Visible existing_faults.tif structure tensors at two smoothing scales (sigma=3 px [300 m] vs sigma=9 px [900 m])
Cached numerical feature stack band 12 (det_elev) Gaussian derivatives and structure-tensor coherence
Visible connected-component length and cross-/along-strike offset frame
candidates.signature: Spin-2 structure-tensor turning discrepancy ||T_fine - T_coarse||_2 and signed bend-wall asymmetry side * (T_fine x T_coarse) at the nearest visible anchor, combined with detrended-elevation scarp tangent alignment cos(2*(theta_scarp - theta_host)).
candidates.why_missing_faults: Restraining and releasing bends along primary faults concentrate off-trace wall-rock stress where slip cannot be accommodated on a planar master surface, nucleating short synthetic splays and wall-rock fracture meshes (Tchalenko 1970; Schreurs 2003; Savage & Brodsky 2011) that 1:250,000 compilations omit after mapping the main range-front fault.
candidates.difference_from_repo: Existing anatomy.py computes trace orientation at a single scale (sigma=3 px) and strand_orientation.py tested only single-scale TMI magnetic tangents (band 14). Multi-scale host-trace turning, signed bend concavity/convexity, and detrended-elevation scarp relative strike had not been implemented or evaluated in this repo.
candidates.non_fault_mimic: Erosional range-front scarps, fluvial terrace margins, and cartographic digitization vertices along sinuous range fronts
candidates.implementation_cost: Low-Medium; CPU only, uses verified local catalogue and cached band 12
candidates.obtainability: Verified: all local catalogue and cached feature bands passed SHA256 checks
candidates.status: TESTED in Experiment 1 (E1); binary HOLDOUT-DTI 0.112331 [0.098505, 0.128094] vs anatomy 0.109647 (+0.002684 [-0.004964, +0.010406]); soft HOLDOUT-DTI 0.023488 vs 0.022876. See relay_bend_holdout.json

candidates.hypothesis: Two-host damage-zone superposition & en echelon relay stepover mechanics
layers: Nearest two DISTINCT visible 8-connected fault components (C1 != C2) from existing_faults.tif via exact 12-bitplane Euclidean distance transforms
Component distances (d1, d2), component lengths (L1, L2), and local strikes (theta1, theta2)
candidates.signature: Relay distance ratio d1 / (d1 + d2) peaking at 0.5 on the medial axis between distinct fault systems, inter-host stepover corridor facing -grad(d1) . grad(d2) in [-1, 1] (+1 inside the corridor between two stepping hosts), inter-host strike agreement cos(2*(theta1 - theta2)), and partnering-host displacement proxy log(1 + L2).
candidates.why_missing_faults: Distributed shear experiments (Schreurs 2003) and northern Walker Lane structural syntheses (Faulds, Henry & Hinz 2005) show that en echelon fault steps are linked by short synthetic/antithetic breaching strands and relay ramps across the stepover corridor between two primary traces. Single-nearest-host models are blind to whether a partnering fault trace sits across strike to form a relay zone.
candidates.difference_from_repo: Every prior model in anatomy.py and strand_orientation.py queried only the single nearest visible pixel via a single EDT. True two-host distinct-component superposition (H57-I in REMAINING_WORK.md §3) was never implemented until this session.
candidates.non_fault_mimic: Unrelated subparallel lithologic contacts or erosional ridge crests bounding an intervening alluvial valley
candidates.expected_improvement: High (qualitative expectation prior to code; directly targets inter-fault stepovers)
candidates.implementation_cost: Medium; exact 12-bitplane EDT separates all 3,199 components without approximation on CPU
candidates.obtainability: Verified: all required catalogue data are local and SHA256-verified
candidates.status: TESTED in Experiment 2 (E2); binary HOLDOUT-DTI 0.135204 [0.119140, 0.153036], beating single-host anatomy by +0.025556 [95% CI +0.013943, +0.037109] and distance-only by +0.022479 [95% CI +0.007867, +0.038463]; soft HOLDOUT-DTI 0.031160 [0.024691, 0.038109]. See relay_bend_holdout.json

candidates.hypothesis: Along-host & inter-host slip-sense transition heterogeneity in Walker Lane transfer zones
layers: Visible matched INGENIOUS RL/LL/N slip-sense records (trace_segments_utm11.csv restricted strictly to visible traces)
1.5 km (15 px) Gaussian densities of strike-slip (RL/LL) and normal (N) visible traces
Two-host relay and host-bend geometry
candidates.signature: Kinematic heterogeneity index 4*rho_SS*rho_N / (rho_SS + rho_N)^2 * presence in [0, 1] peaking where strike-slip (RL/LL) and normal (N) visible faults coexist in transtensional horsetail/relay transfer zones, combined with nearest-host strike-slip handedness (sense_sgn, sense_side).
candidates.why_missing_faults: In the northern Walker Lane / Great Basin transition (Faulds, Henry & Hinz 2005), dextral strike-slip faults terminate or transfer slip into normal fault arrays via dense meshes of short oblique/normal linking strands that are under-represented in regional fault maps.
candidates.difference_from_repo: Earlier session E3 tested only the single nearest pixel's RL/LL sign and treated N (normal) identically to unrecorded (0). Spatial transitions and coexistence between strike-slip and normal faulting were untested.
candidates.non_fault_mimic: Inconsistent catalogue attribution across quadrangle map boundaries
candidates.expected_improvement: Low-Medium; attribute coverage and matching precision are limiting
candidates.implementation_cost: Low once visible-only sense raster and two-host relay geometry are built
candidates.obtainability: Verified: trace_segments_utm11.csv is local and SHA256-verified; official GDR v2 metadata (CC BY 4.0) retrieved
candidates.status: TESTED in Experiment 3 (E3); binary HOLDOUT-DTI 0.141391 [0.124513, 0.161457] (+0.006188 [-0.001694, +0.015702] over E2); soft HOLDOUT-DTI 0.033898 (+0.002738 [+0.000307, +0.005994] over E2). Because the binary paired 95% lower bound (-0.001694) slightly straddles zero, E2 (relay_bend_anatomy) is retained by the predeclared rule.

candidates.hypothesis: Radiometric K/eTh hydrothermal potassium-metasomatism ratio in stepover damage zones
layers: External USGS GeoDAWN airborne gamma-ray spectrometry potassium (%K) and equivalent thorium (eTh ppm) grids
Two-host relay and damage-zone geometry
candidates.signature: Elevated K/eTh ratio along fault damage zones, isolating potassic hydrothermal alteration (adularia/illite clay replacement from geothermal fluid upflow) from primary lithologic thorium variation.
candidates.why_missing_faults: Concealed secondary strands that channel geothermal fluids alter host-rock feldspars to potassium-bearing clays/adularia even where surface fault scarps are eroded or buried by thin alluvial veneer.
candidates.difference_from_repo: The 19-band training_features.tif stack contains magnetic, gravity, elevation, conductivity, geodetic, and seismic layers, but omits the GeoDAWN radiometric K, eTh, eU channels.
candidates.non_fault_mimic: Unfaulted felsic volcanic tuffs,playa evaporites, or arkosic alluvial fans with high primary potassium
candidates.expected_improvement: Low-Medium; radiometric gamma rays sample only the top ~30 cm of regolith
candidates.implementation_cost: High (requires external raw GeoDAWN radiometric grids not in training_features.tif)
candidates.obtainability: Official CC0 source identified (USGS GeoDAWN ScienceBase release, DOI 10.5066/P93LGLVQ), but sciencebase.gov binary storage is outside this sandbox's outbound allowlist; therefore documented as backlog and not run.
candidates.status: BACKLOG; requires external USGS ScienceBase radiometric rasters outside sandbox network allowlist (3-experiment budget used by H57-H, H57-I2, H57-J)

candidates.hypothesis: Candidate magnetic-edge relative strike in the fitted damage zone (Prior Session 3)
layers: Cached numerical feature stack band 14 (tmi)
Visible existing_faults.tif geometry
Recorded INGENIOUS sense where matched
candidates.signature: Gaussian scalar derivatives supply an axial magnetic-edge tangent and coherence; cos(2*(candidate strike - primary strike)) interacts with distance and host length.
candidates.why_missing_faults: A secondary strand may offset magnetized units even when it has no mapped surface trace.
candidates.difference_from_repo: Replaced offset-vector azimuth phi with catalogue-independent magnetic-edge tangent.
candidates.non_fault_mimic: Magnetized dikes, lithologic contacts and east-west airborne leveling stripes
candidates.status: TESTED in Session 3 (negative binary gain: 0.109168 vs 0.112725 distance-only; see run_card_session3_orientation.json)

candidates.hypothesis: Damage-zone *density* decay rather than a hard envelope: fit a power law in strand density vs distance per length bin and allocate dots to the predicted hazard gradient
layers: Visible existing_faults.tif components and their connected-component length
withheld-positive distance distribution per bin (already measured in evidence/h58_structure.json)
candidates.signature: Empirical hazard rate lambda(d | L) = dN/dd / area of the distance annulus, fitted as a truncated power law lambda ~ d**(-b) with b pooled across length bins; allocation weight proportional to expected marginal kernel credit, not to a clipped in/out mask
candidates.why_missing_faults: Mapping completeness falls with distance from a named master trace, so the uncatalogued population is biased toward the far halo; a density law keeps budget there instead of truncating at a fitted edge, which is what the current W(L) envelope does at 0.54 fraction-in-zone
candidates.difference_from_repo: strike_zone.fit_zone returns a binary keep mask (ratio threshold on positive occupancy per distance bin); H58 ships its envelope clipped at W(L). This replaces the clip with the fitted decay itself and lets the allocator trade near against far mass
candidates.expected_improvement: Uncertain. The H58 enrichment curve peaks at 4-5 px and still holds 0.0021 of base rate out to 16-20 px, so a soft tail could buy coverage the clip discards; it could equally spend budget on noise
candidates.implementation_cost: Low: reuses fold_geometry columns and fit_zone's histograms, one new estimator, four folds
candidates.non_fault_mimic: Mapping-effort gradients (density falls where mappers worked less), which look exactly like a decay law

candidates.hypothesis: Fault-tip stress lobes and sibling-relay overlap (the untried H57-B): extrapolate each component's terminal lobes and superpose them where two tips face each other
layers: Visible trace skeleton endpoints and local strike at the last k pixels of each component
12-bitplane exact EDT to the nearest and second-nearest distinct component
candidates.signature: Gaussian lobe centered on each tip, elongated along the tip's local strike, amplitude decaying with the mapped component length; relay term = product of two facing-tip lobes inside a stepover window
candidates.why_missing_faults: Displacement tapers to zero at a tip, so damage concentrates in a lobate pattern past the mapped end; the mapping usually stops at the visible end, which is precisely where uncatalogued strands continue
candidates.difference_from_repo: The repository's relay_bend_anatomy (Session 5) models stepovers between two *parallel* hosts; nothing in the repo builds a tip field. REMAINING_WORK.md lists H57-B as still untried
candidates.expected_improvement: Medium-high: Session 5's two-host relay arm produced the largest holdout gain measured in this repo (+0.0256), and tips are the other geometric singularity
candidates.implementation_cost: Low-medium: endpoints come from the existing component labelling; needs a rotated-Gaussian splat and a facing test
candidates.non_fault_mimic: Erosional pass and range-front notches at valley heads; digitisation truncation of a continuous trace

candidates.hypothesis: Brittle-ductile coupling: predicted secondary-crack density from slip rate and seismogenic thickness (Ben-Zion & Smith 2023 BSSC), used as a spatial prior on the damage-zone budget
layers: InSAR/GNSS slip-rate raster where available
isotherm depth / seismogenic thickness Zbt from a heat-flow model
catalogue-derived component length as before
candidates.signature: N ~ f(slip rate / Zbt) from the BSSC scaling, resampled to the competition grid, entering only as a prior weight on the allocation, never as a hard mask
candidates.why_missing_faults: Damage density scales with accumulated slip, which is set by long-term slip rate times duration; areas of high Zbt or low slip rate have thin damage zones regardless of how good the mapping is
candidates.difference_from_repo: Every feature in the repository today is derived from the provided rasters. This is the first candidate to import an external physical rate field
candidates.expected_improvement: Unknown and possibly nil: the sandbox cannot reach the slip-rate or heat-flow hosts, so the input path itself must be solved first
candidates.implementation_cost: High plus an external-data dependency the owner must supply; blocked by network scope in this workspace
candidates.non_fault_mimic: Spatial variation of seismogenic thickness partly reflects sediment cover and geology, not damage
candidates.status: UNTRIED - blocked: external rate fields are not retrievable in this workspace (flagged, not faked)

candidates.hypothesis: Cross-cutting relative-age graph: prefer strand candidates that truncate or are truncated by mapped traces, because young secondary strands cut older fabric
layers: Visible trace skeleton with junction detection
component adjacency from the existing 8-connected labelling
candidates.signature: Count of T-junctions (a candidate arc terminating against a mapped trace) minus X-junctions, normalised by arc length, per direction bin; enters as a multiplicative gate on the anatomy intensity
candidates.why_missing_faults: Mapping completeness drops for short strands, but a short strand that clearly cuts a mapped fault is high-confidence; truncation is scale-free evidence that survives under-mapping
candidates.difference_from_repo: No junction-topology term exists in the repository: network.py computes strikes and frames, anatomy.py uses distance/orientation, and nothing uses truncation relations
candidates.expected_improvement: Medium: converts the existing skeleton into relational evidence at near-zero data cost
candidates.implementation_cost: Medium: needs a robust junction detector on a 100 m raster; risk of digitisation artefacts dominating
candidates.non_fault_mimic: Intersection with a mapped contact or a dike produces the same T geometry

candidates.hypothesis: Geothermal-specific permeability target: lineament-node centrality where faults cross structural domains, because the scored label is fault presence used as an indicator of geothermal resources
layers: Visible faults + SGMC 100 m geology contacts
cached 19-band GeoDAWN stack (requires .cache/features restore)
node/intersection graph of the combined lineament network
candidates.signature: Betweenness centrality of lineament intersections, weighted by contrast across the contact, projected onto the fault grid
candidates.why_missing_faults: The private labeller adds faults where geomorphology and geophysics both show a lineament, even where no surface trace was mapped; a node measure is blind to trace length
candidates.difference_from_repo: Uses the geology + geophysical cache, which H58 explicitly did not touch, and measures network position instead of local geometry
candidates.expected_improvement: Speculative. The target is fault presence, not temperature or reservoir quality, so a resource-flavoured feature may add nothing
candidates.implementation_cost: Medium, but gated on restoring and hash-verifying the feature cache in-session
candidates.non_fault_mimic: Lithologic contacts and intrusive bodies generate lineaments and high contrast without being faults
candidates.status: UNTRIED - deferred: needs the git-ignored feature cache restored before it can be run
